text: Okay, twelve minutes on the timer, starting now. I'll give you a shout when it's up, so go and do something else for a bit.
Sure, a timer for the eggs. Seven minutes gets you a soft middle, nine if you want them firm all the way through. Which one?
Done, the oven timer is set for forty minutes. I'll remind you at the halfway point too, in case you want to turn the tray.
Got it, your tea timer is going. Four minutes is about right for black tea, any longer and it starts to taste like a punishment.
Your laundry timer just went off. The wash is finished, so if you move it to the dryer now, it won't sit there smelling damp.
Right, I've paused the timer at six minutes left. Just tell me when you're ready and I'll pick it up from exactly where it stopped.
The pasta timer has three minutes to go. If you want to check it early, bite a piece, it should still be a little firm in the middle.
Alright, two timers are running now. The rice has fourteen minutes left and the vegetables have eight, so the veg will finish first.
I've cancelled the bread timer, since you said the loaf came out early. The other one, for the soup, is still running.
Your timer is done! That was the twenty-minute one for the chicken, so it's worth checking it's cooked through before you serve it.
You've got five minutes left on the focus timer. Finish the thought you're on, and then you've earned a proper break.
Sure thing, I'll set a timer for a quarter of an hour. That's fifteen minutes, which should be plenty for the dough to rest.
No problem, the timer's now ninety minutes for the slow roast. I'll check in with you after the first hour, just in case.
That timer has been ringing for a while, so I've silenced it. It was the one for the washing, if you were wondering what it was.
Easy, a three-minute timer for brushing your teeth. I'll tell you when each minute passes so you know you're on track.
Okay, I've added another five minutes to the timer. It'll go off at twenty to eight now instead of a quarter to.
There are no timers running right now. Did you want me to start one, or were you thinking of the alarm for tomorrow?
Timer's named, it's called potatoes now. That way when it goes off you'll know exactly which pot needs your attention.
The cookie timer has ten minutes left. They'll look a little soft when they come out, but they firm up as they cool, trust me.
I've reset the timer back to twenty-five minutes. Let's call this the second round, and maybe put your phone face down this time.
Fine by me, I'll stop all three timers at once. If you need any of them back, I can restart them with whatever time they had left.
Your alarm is set for half past six tomorrow morning. That gives you about seven and a half hours of sleep if you go to bed now.
Alright, I've moved tomorrow's alarm to seven o'clock. Your first meeting isn't until ten, so you may as well sleep in a bit.
Got it, no alarm on Saturday. You'll wake up whenever your body decides, which, based on past weekends, will be quite late.
Your weekday alarm is on for a quarter to seven, every day from Monday to Friday. Weekends are left alone, the way you like it.
Sure, a second alarm ten minutes after the first. It's a backup, so you won't be able to blame me if you sleep through both.
I've switched the alarm sound to the gentle chimes. They start quietly and get louder, which should be kinder than the bell.
Snoozing for nine more minutes. That's the second snooze, though, so I'd get moving after this one if I were you.
Okay, alarm cleared for tomorrow. You're on holiday, so I'll leave the mornings to you until you tell me otherwise.
You have two alarms tomorrow, one at six o'clock and one at twenty past. Do you want to keep both or just the later one?
Done, I've set an alarm for twenty to five. That's very early, so I'll make the sound bright and keep the lights low until you're up.
Tomorrow's alarm is a bit under eight hours away. If you start winding down now, you'll still get a full night's rest out of it.
The alarm for your early train is set for five past five. I've also turned on the hallway light for then, so you won't trip over anything.
I've turned off the repeating alarm for Wednesday evenings. You said that class finished last month, so there's no need to keep waking for it.
Morning! Your alarm's been going for a minute now. It's a quarter past seven, and it's chilly out, so maybe grab a jumper.
Right, the alarm label now says take the bins out. When it rings on Thursday evening, you'll know exactly why.
Okay, alarm tone changed to birdsong. It's a bit cheerful for six in the morning, but you did ask for something softer.
Every alarm you have is off now, including the weekend ones. Just say the word if you want me to put any of them back.
That alarm already rang at ten past six, and you turned it off yourself. You may not remember it, but I promise it happened.
Sure, I'll wake you at half past one with the lights first and the sound after. A slow start should make the nap easier to leave.
Your nap alarm is set for twenty-five minutes from now. Any longer than that and you'll probably wake up groggy instead of rested.
It's a quarter past eight on a Tuesday evening. You don't have anything else in the calendar tonight, so the rest of it is yours.
Right now it's ten to midnight. You told me to nudge you if you were still up at this time, so consider this the nudge.
It's just gone half past three in the afternoon. That's usually when you start to fade, so maybe a glass of water and a short walk.
It's twenty past eleven in the morning. Your call is at noon, so you've got forty minutes to finish what you're doing.
The time is five to nine. If you leave in the next ten minutes, you'll still make it before the shop opens at a quarter past.
It's almost seven o'clock in the evening. The light outside is going, so I've brought the living room lamps up a little.
You've been at your desk for nearly three hours straight. It's half past four now, so a short break would do you some good.
It's twenty-five to six, and the sun comes up in about half an hour. If you want to see it, now's the time to get the kettle on.
It's a little after two in the morning. I won't lecture you, but tomorrow's alarm is at seven, so the maths is not on your side.
Okay, your countdown for the pizza is at ten minutes. Peek through the glass at around eight, the crust can go quickly at the end.
Bread timer is finished, so give the bottom a tap. If it sounds hollow, it's done, and if not, give it another five minutes.
I've started a timer for the laundry and another for the dishwasher. The laundry ends at a quarter to three, the dishes about an hour later.
Of course, a timer for your plants. Thirty seconds of watering each should be enough, and I'll tell you when to move on to the next one.
Your presentation practice timer is set for eight minutes. Try to finish with a minute to spare, that way nerves won't push you over.
Steak timer started, three minutes on this side. Don't press it down with the spatula, it squeezes out all the good stuff.
That's the last timer finished for the evening. Everything that was cooking should be done now, so it's time to eat.
Want me to set a timer for your stretches? I can count off thirty seconds for each one so you don't have to watch the clock.
Yep, the timer is still running, eleven minutes to go. I'll let you know as soon as it's up, so don't worry about keeping track.
Here's the plan for the roast. The potatoes go in at six o'clock and the meat comes out at half past, and I've set timers for both.
The stopwatch is running. You asked me to time how long the walk to the station takes, so just tell me when you get there.
Stopwatch stopped at twelve minutes and forty seconds. That's a good minute faster than last week, so whatever you did, keep doing it.
Your run today took thirty-one minutes. That's your quickest this month, though I suspect the downhill finish helped a little.
Lap recorded, that was four minutes and ten seconds. The second lap is usually your slowest, so try to keep this pace going.
I've cleared the stopwatch. If you want to time something else, just say start and I'll begin counting straight away.
Sure, I'll count you down from ten for the photo. Everyone should be in place by the time I get to three, so tell them to squeeze in.
Okay, a sixty-second countdown for the plank. You can do it, and I'll call out the last ten seconds so you know the end is close.
The rice needs another seven minutes, then leave it covered off the heat for five more. I've set one timer that covers both parts.
You set a timer earlier for the car park, and it's going off now. You've got about ten minutes before the ticket runs out.
Just so you know, the pressure cooker timer finished a minute ago. Give it ten minutes to release on its own before you open the lid.
Your meditation timer is done. Take a breath before you get up, there's nothing on the calendar for the next half hour anyway.
That was a long one, ninety minutes of focus. I'd stop the timer here and take a real break before you start on anything new.
Alright, timer extended by a minute. The caramel can turn from golden to burnt very fast, so keep an eye on the colour.
The bath is filling now, and I've set a timer for eight minutes. I'll remind you to turn off the tap, you know what happened last time.
Your charging reminder is set for forty-five minutes. That should get the phone to full without leaving it plugged in all night.
The timer for screen time is on, an hour from now. I'll give a ten-minute warning first, so it doesn't come as a sudden shock.
The slow cooker has been on for six hours now. Two more and the stew should be ready, so I'll check in with you at around seven o'clock.
It's a quarter to ten, and your favourite show starts at ten. That's just enough time to make a cup of tea and settle in.
Over where your brother lives, it's twenty past six in the morning. I'd wait at least an hour or two before you call him.
Okay, I'll ring an alarm at noon to remind you to eat. You skipped lunch twice this week, and I noticed, so this is me caring.
Your alarm tomorrow is earlier than usual, a quarter past five. I've set the coffee machine to start at five as well, so it's ready.
Alarm's set for the airport run, ten to four in the morning. It's horrible, I know, but at least the roads will be empty.
Okay, from now on your weekend alarm is nine o'clock. Early enough to have a morning, late enough to feel like a weekend.
I've pushed the alarm back by a quarter of an hour, so it's now at five to seven. Just this once, though, don't make it a habit.
You've snoozed three times already. It's twenty-five past seven, and if you don't get up now, breakfast is going to be a banana on the bus.
Sure, the alarm will play your morning playlist instead of a tone. Music first, then the lights, so you wake up a bit more gently.
Your Sunday alarm is still set from last week. Do you want to keep it for eight, or should I turn it off and let you sleep?
Got you, an alarm at a quarter past three for the delivery window. I'll also let you know if the doorbell goes before then.
The alarm on the bedroom speaker is off, but the one in the kitchen is still on. Did you want both of them silenced?
Rise and shine! It's seven o'clock, the kettle's on, and it's going to be sunny all day. Not a bad start, honestly.
Good morning. It's half past six, and you slept a bit less than usual, so go easy on yourself today. Coffee first, emails later.
Morning, it's a quarter to eight and raining. Your first thing today is at half past nine, so there's no rush, take your time.
It's twenty to eight and you're still in bed, which is fine on a Saturday. I'll keep the blinds closed for another half hour.
I'll wake you at six with the lights only, no sound. You said the alarm made you jump yesterday, so we'll try it the quiet way.
That alarm is a repeating one, every second Tuesday. It's for the recycling collection, if you were wondering why it's so odd.
Okay, alarm deleted. That was the one called old gym class, and it hasn't been useful in months, so I'm glad to see it go.
Fair enough, I'll keep the alarm but change the label to something more polite. Wake up, please, is now what it says.
Alarms for the week are all set, seven o'clock on workdays and nine on the weekend. Thursday is earlier because of the dentist.
You've got six hours and twenty minutes until the alarm goes. If you're still reading, maybe make this the last chapter.
Got it, an alarm every hour from nine until five to remind you to stand up. It'll be a soft tap, nothing that'll disturb a call.
It's a quarter past four. The light will start to go in about an hour, so if you wanted that walk, I'd head out soon.
It's twenty to one, nearly lunchtime. You said you'd make something proper today instead of eating at your desk again.
Half past nine already, the morning's flying. You've got your call at ten, and the notes you need are still open on the laptop.
It's just about midnight, a few seconds to go. Happy birthday, by the way! I wanted to be the first one to say it.
It's ten past two in the afternoon. You've been on that spreadsheet since breakfast, so it might be time to look at something else.
It's five to five on a Friday. I'd say you can start winding down, nobody sends anything important at this time anyway.
It's a quarter to midnight, and the house is quiet. I've turned off everything except the hall light, so you can find your way up.
It's twenty-five past three in the morning, which is far too early to be awake. Do you want some quiet rain sounds to help you drift off?
It's almost six, and the sun is setting. If you go out on the balcony in the next ten minutes, the sky should be at its best.
It's eleven o'clock on the dot. The bakery closes at noon on a Sunday, so if you want fresh bread, now's your chance.
Your sister's evening is just starting, she's about five hours behind you. If you call now, you'll catch her before dinner.
There are twelve days until your holiday. I know you're counting, so I'll keep a quiet countdown going on the kitchen screen.
It's three weeks to the day until the wedding. If you still need to find a gift, this weekend would be a good time to look.
Your birthday is on a Thursday this year, nine days from now. Want me to keep the evening clear in the calendar?
It's been forty minutes since you put the washing on. It should be on the final spin now, so it'll be finished in about five.
You left the oven on about twenty minutes ago. There's nothing in it, as far as I can tell, so I've turned it off for you.
Your parking ends at half past two, which is in fifteen minutes. If you're still in the shop, now's the time to head back.
The library books are due back on Friday. That's in two days, so I'll remind you tomorrow evening to put them by the door.
That's the third time you've asked me the time in ten minutes. Are you waiting for something, or just very bored?
Okay, I'll count the minutes until the pizza arrives. The estimate was half an hour, and it's been twenty, so not long now.
Fine, I'll leave the timer running in the background and stay quiet. You won't hear from me until the cake is ready.
Timer set for twenty minutes, then I'll dim the lights to remind everyone it's bedtime for the little one. Story time starts now.
You wanted a warning before the shops close. It's half past five, and most of them shut at six, so there's still a little time.
Your tea has been steeping for eight minutes now. That's double what you wanted, so it might be strong enough to stand a spoon in.
The kettle boiled a few minutes ago. If you're making green tea, let it cool for another minute or two, it tastes less bitter.
Your countdown says it's two days and four hours until the concert. I've also put a reminder to charge your phone the night before.
I can set a timer for that, but how long were you thinking? For a short nap I'd say twenty minutes, for a proper rest an hour.
Your morning routine timer is running. Shower first, five minutes, then breakfast, and I'll call out each step as you go.
Ten minutes until the guests arrive. The oven's on, the music's playing, and you still have flour on your cheek, just so you know.
Okay, starting a timer that repeats every twenty minutes. Each time it goes off, get up and walk around the room for a moment.
The dryer will be done at ten past four. Take the shirts out straight away and hang them, then you won't have to iron anything.
I've put a fifteen-minute timer on the porch light. It'll stay on while you bring the shopping in, then switch itself off.
That timer was for the bread proving, and it's done. The dough should have roughly doubled, and if not, give it another twenty minutes.
Do you want the timer to keep going after it rings, so you can see how long it's been? That's useful for things like roasting.
You asked for a nudge in an hour, and here it is. It's a quarter to three, and you said you'd move the car before then.
Two minutes left on the toast timer. I know it says two, but your toaster is enthusiastic, so maybe stand nearby.
Okay, two egg timers running side by side. Four minutes for yours, six for the hard one, and I'll call each of them out separately.
Got it, I'll wake you up at the end of the film if you fall asleep. It's about two hours long, so that'll be around eleven o'clock.
It's a quarter past ten and the dishwasher's finished. If you empty it now, tomorrow morning will start with a clean kitchen.
Your alarm went off but you were already up, so I've stopped it. Look at you, beating the alarm on a Monday.
Today is Wednesday the fourteenth. You're halfway through the week, and the hard part, your Monday meetings, is already behind you.
Tomorrow is the first of the month. That's when the bins move to the new schedule, so I'll remind you on Tuesday night instead of Wednesday.
The clocks go back this weekend, on Sunday morning. You'll get an extra hour in bed, and I'll change all your alarms for you.
Next Friday is the twenty-first. I've checked, and you've got nothing on that evening yet, so it's free if you want it.
It's the last day of March today. Spring is properly here, and the evenings should start to feel longer from now on.
Your appointment is in exactly one week, next Tuesday at twenty past nine. I'll remind you the day before and again that morning.
You asked how many days until the end of term. There are seventeen school days left, not counting the bank holiday.
It's a short week, only four working days because of the holiday on Monday. That gives you one less day to do the same amount, sorry.
This Saturday is the longest day of the year. Sunset isn't until a quarter past nine, so you could easily have dinner outside.
Sunrise tomorrow is at twenty to seven, and sunset is at ten past five. That's about ten and a half hours of daylight to work with.
It's eleven degrees and cloudy at the moment. It should warm up to about sixteen by the afternoon, so a light jacket will do.
Looks like rain from about three o'clock. If you're heading out, take the big umbrella, the small one gave up last time.
Tomorrow will be sunny and warm, around twenty-four degrees. A good day to get the washing out on the line, if you ask me.
Frost tonight, it's going down to two below zero. I'd bring the herbs inside, and maybe give the car a few extra minutes in the morning.
Right now it's drizzly and grey, about nine degrees. Not dreadful, but you'll want something waterproof if you're walking.
The wind is picking up this evening, gusts of about forty miles an hour. I'd bring the garden chairs in before you go to bed.
It's going to be a scorcher, thirty-one degrees by mid afternoon. Keep the blinds down on the sunny side and drink plenty of water.
There's a chance of thunderstorms later, mostly after six. If you were planning a run, this morning would be the better window.
No rain at all this week, which is rare. The garden will need watering every evening, though, so I'll remind you around eight.
Snow is forecast overnight, maybe a few centimetres by morning. Leave a bit earlier tomorrow, the roads will be slow.
Today's high is nineteen and the low is eight. It'll feel colder in the shade, so bring a jumper even if it looks bright.
The fog should lift by about ten o'clock. Until then visibility is poor, so take it slow if you're driving this morning.
It's warmer outside than inside right now, twenty-two out there and nineteen in here. Want me to open the windows a bit?
Showers on and off all afternoon, nothing heavy. It's the kind of day where you'll get damp but probably not soaked.
This weekend looks lovely, dry and mild on both days. Saturday is a little warmer, around twenty, if you want to plan something outside.
Hold on before you hang the washing out, rain is due in about forty minutes. Maybe use the rack inside today instead.
It's freezing out there, literally, zero degrees on the dot. The pavement will be icy, so take the steps by the side gate carefully.
The humidity is high today, so it's going to feel sticky even though it's only twenty-three. A fan in the bedroom tonight might help.
It'll be bright and breezy tomorrow, about fifteen degrees. Not quite shorts weather, but you could get away with a light top.
The forecast for your trip says rain on Friday and sun on Saturday. I'd pack a waterproof and a pair of sunglasses, just to cover it.
The pollen count is high again today. If your eyes were itchy yesterday, it might be worth keeping the windows shut this afternoon.
Wet start, dry finish. The rain stops at around eleven, and the afternoon should be clear, with a bit of sunshine after lunch.
Overnight it's dropping to four degrees. I've set the heating to come on at six, so the house will be warm when you get up.
There's a weather warning for strong winds tonight. Nothing dramatic, but the bins might go for a walk if you leave them out.
You asked if you need a coat. Yes, it's eight degrees with a cold wind, so it'll feel more like four once you're out there.
It's a beautiful evening, still and clear, around eighteen degrees. The stars should be good tonight if you want to sit outside.
Rain is coming in from the west and should reach us in about an hour. If you're cycling home, now is the time to leave.
Tomorrow starts cold, about three degrees, but gets up to twelve by the afternoon. Layers are the answer, as usual.
Sunny all day but very windy, so it'll feel colder than the thermometer says. Hats will be a challenge, hold on to yours.
Heavy rain overnight, about a month's worth in one go, they're saying. The low road by the river might flood, so take the hill route.
It's warm enough for the barbecue, twenty-six and no rain until late evening. Light it at six and you'll have plenty of time.
The temperature's been falling all afternoon. It's down to seven degrees now, and I've nudged the heating up by one.
It's a mixed bag this week. Monday and Tuesday wet, Wednesday dry, and the weekend is still too far out to call with any confidence.
Thinking about a picnic? Saturday is the better day, dry and around twenty degrees. Sunday has showers from mid morning onwards.
Clear skies tonight and a full moon. If you can't sleep, at least the view from the bedroom window should be worth it.
The rain has stopped for now, but there's more on the way at about five. If you want that walk, the next hour is your gap.
Hail is possible this afternoon, mostly short bursts. I'd move the car under the carport if it's parked out on the drive.
Your weather for today, cool and cloudy, high of fourteen. No rain expected, so the umbrella can stay at home for once.
It's muggy and close outside, the kind of air that usually means a storm later. I'll warn you if it looks like it's getting near.
Tomorrow will be the warmest day of the week, nearly thirty. I'd water the tomatoes early, before the sun gets on them.
The snow is melting quickly, it's above freezing now at five degrees. The paths will be slushy rather than icy, which is a relief.
It's raining heavily, so I've closed the skylight. The forecast says it eases off around nine, if you can wait until then.
I checked the forecast for the race on Sunday. Cool, overcast and dry, about twelve degrees, which is just about perfect for running.
A cold front is coming through this afternoon. The temperature will drop by six or seven degrees in an hour, so dress for later, not now.
No frost tonight, it stays around six degrees. The car should be fine in the morning without any scraping.
Sunny spells and a light breeze, a very pleasant twenty-one degrees. If you've got a window between calls, it's a lovely afternoon to sit out.
Weather's looking grim for the weekend, I'm afraid. Rain on Saturday, rain on Sunday, and wind on both. A good weekend for a film.
It's dry for now, but the radar shows a band of showers about twenty minutes away. Washing in, windows shut, just to be safe.
Even though it's sunny, it's only eight degrees. Don't let the blue sky fool you, it's properly cold out there.
That's the third grey day in a row, I know. The good news is that Thursday finally looks bright, with sun for most of the day.
You have three things on today. A call at ten, lunch with your sister at one, and the gym at six, if you still feel like it by then.
Your afternoon is clear, nothing until the dinner at seven. If you wanted time to focus, this is probably the best chance all week.
Tomorrow starts early, with the team meeting at half past eight. I'd lay your things out tonight so the morning is less of a scramble.
Okay, I've added dinner with your parents on Saturday at seven. Want me to block out the afternoon as well, for the drive over?
There's a clash on Thursday. The dentist is at two, and the project review is at a quarter past two. Which one would you like to move?
Done, the meeting is moved to Friday at eleven. I've kept the same room and the same invite list, so nobody else needs to do anything.
Your next appointment is the haircut at four. It's a twenty-minute walk, so you'll want to leave by about twenty to.
Nothing in the calendar for Sunday at all. A properly empty day, which, honestly, you haven't had in about a month.
You've got back-to-back calls from nine until one. I've put a short gap in the middle so you can at least make a cup of tea.
Sure, I'll put the school play on Wednesday evening at six. I've also added a reminder in the morning to bring the costume.
The plumber said he'd come between eight and noon on Monday. I've blocked the whole morning, since those windows are never exact.
Your week at a glance, busy Monday and Tuesday, quieter from Wednesday, and Friday is completely free. Not bad, really.
I've cancelled the book club on Tuesday and let the group know. I said something had come up, nothing more specific than that.
You have a call with your manager in fifteen minutes. The notes from last time are open on the laptop if you want a quick look.
Next week is a lot. Five evening events, and two of them are on the same night. Do you want me to help you pick which ones to drop?
Okay, the party's in the calendar for the twelfth, from eight until late. I've left the next morning empty, just in case.
The car's service is booked for Thursday morning at nine. You'll need to drop it off by a quarter to, and they'll call when it's ready.
You asked when you last saw the dentist. It was in May, about six months ago, so you're due for a check-up soon.
There's a free slot on Wednesday between two and four. That would work for the call with the landlord, if you want me to suggest it.
Your flight on Friday leaves at ten past seven in the evening. I'd aim to leave the house at about half past four to be safe.
That event is all day on Saturday, from nine until six. I've moved your usual Saturday run to Sunday morning instead.
The meeting you're thinking of was last Tuesday, not this one. You're free today at that time, so there's nothing to miss.
Yes, the gym class is still on tonight at half past six. The instructor is the one you like, so it should be a good one.
I've put a hold on Thursday afternoon for the move. Nothing is confirmed yet, but at least nobody can book you for something else.
You've accepted the invite for the leaving drinks on Friday. It starts at half past five, a short walk from the office.
Your calendar for tomorrow is empty until eleven. A slow morning for once, so maybe make yourself a real breakfast.
I've set the meeting to repeat every Monday at ten, for the next eight weeks. If it ends earlier, just tell me and I'll stop it.
Your parents' anniversary is on the ninth. That's next Sunday, so if you're sending a card, it should go in the post by Wednesday.
The school pickup is at a quarter past three today, not half past, because of the early finish. I've moved your reminder to match.
You don't have to be anywhere until two. That's four hours, enough to finish the report and still have lunch somewhere nice.
Shall I move the dentist to next week? There's an opening on Tuesday at twenty to ten, and your morning is clear that day.
Okay, I've put the call with the council on Monday at noon. I'll remind you to have the letter in front of you before it starts.
Your evening is booked from six. Dinner, then the film at a quarter past eight, then home, if you're sensible, which you rarely are.
The visitor parking pass needs renewing on the first. I've added it to your calendar, with a reminder the day before.
That appointment was at three, and it's twenty past now. Do you want me to call and see if they can still fit you in?
All set, the video call with your old flatmates is on Sunday at four. I've added a reminder to make a drink and be early for once.
You've got the whole of next week off. I've turned off the work reminders until the Monday after, so nothing will bother you.
You asked what's on Friday. The morning is meetings, the afternoon is free, and the evening is the quiz at the pub at eight.
The conference is three days, Tuesday to Thursday. I've cleared your usual meetings for those days and let people know you're away.
I've moved lunch with your friend to half past twelve, since she asked for a bit earlier. Same place, just a little sooner.
Busy day tomorrow. Six things in the calendar, and the first one is at a quarter to eight, so maybe an early night tonight.
Your check-up is on Tuesday at ten past nine. It's the routine one, so there's nothing you need to bring except yourself.
There are two birthdays this week, your cousin on Wednesday and your neighbour on Saturday. Want me to add gifts to the shopping list?
Okay, the volunteer shift is in. Saturday mornings from nine till twelve, every other week, starting this weekend.
I'd leave for the interview by twenty past one. It's at two, and the bus can be slow at that time of day.
Free evenings this week are Tuesday and Thursday. If you want to see your friends, either of those would work nicely.
The meeting tomorrow got moved to the afternoon, half past three. The organiser sent the change this morning, and I've updated it.
Parents' evening at school is on Thursday at six. You've booked a ten-minute slot with each teacher, and I've put them all in order.
I've added the concert to the calendar, Friday the twentieth, doors at seven. Want a reminder to sort out the tickets on your phone?
You have nothing scheduled for the rest of the day. It's a good time to tackle the pile of post on the table, if you're feeling brave.

Your weekly call with your mum is tonight at eight. I'll ring a soft chime at five to, so you're ready with a cup of tea.
Your calendar says you're on the school run tomorrow. Leave by twenty past eight and you'll get there with a few minutes to spare.
Okay, the holiday is in. Ten days from the third, and I've set a reminder for the day before you go to sort out your out of office.
You haven't replied to the dinner invite for Saturday. Do you want me to accept it, or are you still deciding?
I've blocked off two hours on Wednesday morning for deep work. No meetings will land there unless you say they can.
